messages:
morgan: Quick question — our per-route error UX is ambiguous when we fallback to lower-tier models. Customers see `503` and a generic `fallback` message but not the reason. Can we standardize an error taxonomy + attach trace IDs so the console links directly to runbooks? cc @sam

sam: Two pieces: machine-level cause (OVERLOAD / QUOTA / ROUTE_DOWN) and a user-facing hint. We should add `error.code` and `error.hint` in the response body. Example: `{"status":503, "error": {"code":"ROUTE_OVERLOAD","hint":"Temporarily degraded — request will be retried"}}`

ellie: +1. Important: use an opaque header for traces (eg `x-rw-trace`) instead of hostnames. Console can map trace -> internal span link. Also consider `x-rw-retry-after` when we throttle.

pete: SDK note: keep backward compat. Continue returning 503; add new fields so SDKs can map to typed exceptions. Propose `x-rw-fail-mode` header too.

sam: For telemetry, tag metrics with `route_id` and `fail_mode` so dashboards show fallback rate per route. Add a `fallback_pct` metric on the per-route dashboard.

morgan: Runbooks — can we auto-surface a runbook link for `error.code` (eg https://console.redwood/runbooks/ROUTE_OVERLOAD) in the customer console? That would reduce support noise.

ellie: Privacy check: runbook links should only be visible in the authenticated console. Public endpoints should only show a generic hint. Also redact any infra identifiers in the error.hint.

sam: Draft RFC idea (minimal contract): HTTP status + `error.code` (string) + `error.hint` (string) + headers: `x-rw-trace` (opaque id), `x-rw-retry-after` (seconds, optional).

pete: Migration: rollout in two phases. 1) alpha opt-in header `x-rw-expose-error-v2: true` for a month. 2) make fields stable and GA. SDKs should default to old behavior until they opt-in.

deploy-bot: deploy: canary started on `canary/route-mapping` (build 8351) :rocket:

morgan: Sounds good. Can someone sketch the API spec + console mapping PR? I'll put this on the sprint board. :thumbsup:
